transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’ve started going out of my way to avoid any job that involves getting up high, and when I can’t avoid it I’m barely able to stay up there long enough to do my work. It's really starting to impact my livelihood, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone.
When you are in high places, do you feel an intense fear specifically of falling, or is it more of a fear that you might lose control and intentionally jump?

It's definitely a fear of falling, not any urge to jump. Ever since I watched my coworker's near-fall from the scaffolding, my mind just flashes to pictures of me going over the edge. I get this terrifying feeling that I'm going to lose my balance and tip forward into the empty air.
When you are in those high places, do you experience physical symptoms like a racing heart, dizziness, trembling, or shortness of breath?

Yes, absolutely. The second I step out there, my heart starts pounding like crazy, my chest gets incredibly tight, and my legs turn to pure jelly. I start sweating through my clothes and feel like I'm about to tip right over the edge, even when I know I'm clipped in and safe.
